artifact.title: Soundcheck from both sides of the stage
artifact.summary: Adjust the two mixes independently. The monitor feed branches before the main vocal fader.

nodes.label: Vocal mic
nodes.alt: Handheld microphone with grille and cable

nodes.label: Pre-fader split
nodes.alt: A mixer channel branching before its fader

nodes.label: Floor monitor
nodes.alt: An angled wedge facing the singer

frames.label: Soundcheck
frames.caption: The same vocal enters both branches.

frames.label: Main fader raised
frames.caption: The audience hears more vocal. The monitor stays at soundcheck level.

frames.label: Monitor send raised
frames.caption: The singer hears more vocal. The audience stays at soundcheck level.

frames.label: Both raised
frames.caption: Each mix has been raised by its own control.

evidence.passage: At a small gig, the singer’s microphone feeds two mixes. One goes to the audience through the main speakers. The other goes to the singer through a floor monitor. During soundcheck, the audience hears a clear vocal, but the singer can barely hear herself. The engineer raises only the monitor send. Now the singer hears more voice while the audience mix stays the same. During the chorus, the engineer raises only the main vocal fader. This time the audience hears the lift and the singer’s monitor stays where it was. The monitor send is taken before the main fader, which is what makes those two changes independent.

claims.label: Why the mixes can change independently
quotes: The monitor send is taken before the main fader

name: An evidence desk with a joint reveal

artifact.title: What can the cinema put on record?
artifact.summary: Bring the public notice and the projectionist’s log into evidence. See which details you can substantiate.

blocks.heading: Public notice
blocks.text: The screening was cancelled because of a projector fault. The notice gives no time.

blocks.heading: Projectionist’s log
blocks.text: The lamp failed at 7:12 pm. The log does not record whether the screening went ahead.

blocks.heading: Supported together
blocks.text: The log dates the lamp failure to 7:12 pm. The notice independently records the cancellation due to a projector fault.
Neither source records when the audience was told.

evidence.passage: A cinema’s public notice says the screening was cancelled because of a projector fault. It gives no time. The projectionist’s log records a lamp failure at 7:12 pm. The log does not say whether the show went ahead. Neither source says when the audience was told.
